messages:
jordan: Heads up — customer on prod reported seeing another org's saved query briefly after rapid org-switching in the console. repro: click org A -> quickly switch to org B -> open Saved Searches. :eyes:

nina: Yikes. Any screenshots or console logs?

jordan: have a screenshot, but more useful i grabbed network + proxy logs. snippet:
```
GET /api/console/saved-searches?org_id=org-b
Host: console.redwood.ai
X-Org-Id: org-b
X-Request-Id: req-9f8b
Proxy-Cache: HIT from sidecar-12 (key: /api/console/saved-searches|org-a)
```

kyle: that looks like the cache key is still including old org id in some sidecars. we changed affinity in the last rollout (rev a1b2c3) to use `session_id` for routing/quota which may have unintentionally decoupled cache invalidation from `X-Org-Id`. :face_with_monocle:

samir: that tradeoff was intentional for quota stickiness, but forgot to standardize cache-key normalization. if a session_id persists across quick org swaps, sidecar might return stale payloads for the new org.

jordan: repro frequency ~1/50 rapid switches in my test, shows wrong rows for ~1-2s then refresh corrects. customer hit it once and raised incident.

nina: can someone grep proxy logs for mismatched `X-Org-Id` vs session->org mapping for the trace id? req-9f8b is one. also check if telemetry tags got attributed to wrong org.

kyle: doing a quick grep now. found a cluster of hits where proxy_cache_key was built from `$cookie_session` but the cached object still contains `org-a` payload. nginx snippet from sidecar config:
```
proxy_set_header X-Org-Id $http_x_org_id;
proxy_cache_key "$scheme$host$uri|$cookie_session";
```

kyle: oops — backend rendering still uses the `X-Org-Id` header to scope content, but cache_key excludes it. so when session is sticky across fast switches, cached pages for previous org are reused.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollout rev a1b2c3 -> sidecar/cluster-3 at 2024-10-02T12:34:12Z (info: changed routing affinity to session_id)

samir: that explains it. the fix options: (1) include X-Org-Id in cache key, (2) add a guard in console prefetch to verify the cached payload's org matches session's org, or (3) invalidate session-level caches on org switch.

nina: priority p0 for data isolation. i think (2) is the fastest mitigant while kyle prepares longer-term patch. assign to kyle?

kyle: will do. i'll open a PR to add a runtime guard in the prefetch handler: if cached_payload.org_id != user_session.org_id -> skip cache and fetch fresh, and emit metric `prefetch.cache_org_mismatch`

jordan: filed GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal/issues/4872 with repro + trace IDs. adding logs to capture `cached_org` vs `session_org` for telemetry.

samir: also add a dashboard alert (console:org-mismatch-rate) so SRE can catch regressions. avoid attributing telemetry to wrong org.

nina: one more ask — double-check rollout canary policy. if sidecar change is staged by session affinity only in some clusters, we need to roll back or patch quickly.

kyle: rolling a hotfix PR now, quick guard + metric + unit test. will roll to canary cluster and monitor.

jordan: thanks team. i'll update the customer and mark incident P0 until fix is live. :thumbsup:
